analysis.title: Americas Branded Consumer Goods: Apparel & Accessories: Monthly brand momentum tracker update
key_insights: Net purchase intent (NPI) across GS apparel and accessories coverage softened in October, and net promoter scores stayed muted.
Consumer views of selection, brands, and value improved sequentially in October. Selection driver Y/Y reached 3.0%, brands 1.3%, value 1.2%.
Y/Y purchase intent improved for GAP, Jimmy Choo, Ralph Lauren, Macy's, Ross, and Marshalls.
Purchase intent softened at Urban Outfitters, Under Armour, Free People, and Tommy Hilfiger. Athletic and footwear brands remained muted.
Google Trends Y/Y search growth was strongest at Arc'teryx, Salomon, and Savers. Urban Outfitters, Vans, and lululemon had the largest Y/Y declines.
Sequential search momentum improved most at Arc'teryx, Timberland, and Savers, and weakened most at Helly Hansen, Salomon, and Canada Goose.
FIGS NPI strengthened and now leads specialty peers, while Urban Outfitters and Free People decelerated.
Off-price NPI generally improved, led by Ross and Marshalls, with HomeGoods slightly softer. GS notes Ross's search spike was driven by non-core engagement.
Department store NPI improved at Macy's and Bloomingdale's, Kohl's stable, but search trends softened in recent weeks.
Hardgoods: Ninja NPI slightly softer, and Ninja search stayed positive while YETI and Shark fell below year-ago levels.
Price driver Y/Y improved to -0.6% in October from -1.7% in September, while website/app remained the weakest driver at -2.4%.
GS cautions Google Trends data is noisy and inconsistent, so directional changes are more informative than absolute levels.

market_movers.rationale: Y/Y net purchase intent improved sequentially in October.
Ralph Lauren purchase intent improved and search trends stayed relatively resilient.
Macy's NPI improved in October, though department store search softened.
Ross NPI improved, but the search spike was driven by non-core engagement.
Marshalls NPI improved, though T.J. Maxx and Marshalls search momentum softened.
NPI softened and Google search had the largest Y/Y decline in the coverage set.
Under Armour purchase intent softened in October.
Tommy Hilfiger NPI moderated in October.
Search had among the largest Y/Y declines, though the decline normalized sequentially.
Vans search weakened further and was among the largest Y/Y decliners.
FIGS NPI strengthened to lead specialty peers and search stayed strong.

sector_views.rationale: Aggregate purchase intent softened and NPS is muted, while selection, brands, and value drivers improved. Dispersion by brand is high.

risk_factors: Google Trends data is noisy and inconsistent, so absolute levels are less reliable.
Aggregate net purchase intent deceleration and muted NPS could signal weaker consumer demand.
Website/app driver remains negative Y/Y at -2.4% in October.
Search interest can be driven by non-core engagement, as with Ross.
